predecessors.name: Kingdom of Arles
predecessors.text: the county of Orange, a fief of the Holy Roman Empire raised to a principality by Frederick I in 1163

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the principality, 'ceded to France' under the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 (infobox 'Succeeded by: Kingdom of France')

ledger.x: 1163: Frederick I raises the county of Orange to a principality, held as a fief of the Holy Roman Empire. infobox 'Principality status granted: 1163'; the article's history says Frederick I raised the county to a principality that year.
1393: the principality passes from the Baux to the Chalons.
1713: the Treaty of Utrecht ends the contest.

wars.name: French conquest and occupations of Orange
wars.outcome: Captured by Louis XIV's forces in 1672 and again in August 1682; occupied by France in 1673, 1679, 1690, 1697 and 1702-1713, and ceded to France in 1713 under the Treaty of Utrecht, the Prussian king keeping the title.

certainty.note: A 140-280 km2 enclave: the boundaries are communal and no page gives a boundary line.
